Sunday, July 26.topic: The Montparnasse algorithm for RNA design
Sunday, July 26.speaker: Prof. Tristan Cazenave
Sunday, July 26.abstract: RNA design consists of discovering a nucleotide sequence that optimizes predefined criteria, such as secondary structure. It is useful for synthetic biology, medicine, and nanotechnology. We propose Montparnasse, a Monte Carlo search framework based on Generalized Nested Rollout Policy Adaptation, augmented with a problem-specific prior, slow and long adaptation at level 1, and a lexicographic multicriteria evaluation. Montparnasse solves all 100 puzzles of the Eterna100 V1 benchmark consistently faster than DesiRNA, the previous state of the art, across all time limits, reaching full coverage more than three times faster overall. On messenger RNA secondary structure optimization for hemoglobin alpha, it identifies sequences with more paired bases than the MFE-optimal solution of LinearDesign.

Sunday, July 26.topic: Composite fine-tuning of pre-trained RNA language models for secondary structure prediction
Sunday, July 26.speaker: Arnuv Modh
Sunday, July 26.abstract: This presentation describes an AI pipeline for RNA secondary structure prediction using attention maps from pretrained RNA language models. By extracting where the model “focuses” across nucleotide pairs, the project converts attention patterns into features for machine learning models such as Random Forest, MLP, and XGBoost. Optimized decoding, class weighting, and validation improved prediction accuracy and helped identify biologically meaningful RNA pairing relationships.

Sunday, July 26.speaker: Thomas Karagianes
Sunday, July 26.abstract: This talk explores the landscape of RNA design and optimization machine learning algorithms, and examines how Eterna can best integrate these new tools to support our players and make them better RNA designers. We'll focus on the recently integrated Ribotree algorithm for DegScore optimization and what we learned from players about adding these tools to Eterna.
